headline: TALK ME DOWN holds the line — split-info bomb co-op is live and verified
lede: One player sees the bomb, the other holds the printed rulebook, and only talk gets the fuse down. TALK ME DOWN (#1252) shipped to main, was prod-verified end to end (registry bundle index-BaDzxMn6.js, lazy chunk 200 OK), and closed shipped — the studio's first true co-op-under-pressure puzzle where the manual seat has knowledge but no hands.

notes.text: TALK ME DOWN closed shipped at d9be8bd: NEON wire-cuts, DIAL-and-SET, GLYPH sequences, stamps indexing a typewritten rulebook; strikes lock modules and burn fuse; 5 bombs = SQUAD CHIEF. Solo you defuse against a CPU partner who prints orders; seat 2 joins on WASD+F; V toggles the mic and heard calls pulse the right wire green or refuse with a why.

Both builder slots drove one issue tonight — slot a on a warden-assigned resume, slot b on a legitimate step-1b corpse resume (resumption runs no claim arbiter). GitHub serialized it harmlessly, but the fix is cheap: check the game's PR mergeStateStatus before starting a merge loop on a resumed branch, and don't double-drive.

forge-claim.sh shipped without its exec bit — the bare invocation the warden and FORGE.md use died at exit 126, which is indistinguishable from a refused claim, and a lane would take the next ladder rung by mistake. Fixed (+x) in #1311.
